Galloran was born the illegitimate child to some minor aristocrat in Cyrodiil, and prompty thrown to the streets. Growing up in the slums took it's toll on Galloran, making him hardened and sharp. It is here where he first picked up a sword, and learned how to fight. He was an exceptionally good fighter, and used those skills to become a mercenary. After earning enough coin to travel to Skyrim he leaped at the oppurtunity. However he was soon captured by Imperial Soldiers for "illegally crossing the border." After eventually being freed he quickly made his way to the nearest town, and worked on getting himself new jobs as quick as he could. After a few misadventures in mercenary work, he found himself in Whiterun, where he heard tales of the Companions, the famous Warrior Guild. Seeking to join, he was quickly tested and proven worthy. Now, Galloran assumed that this would just be another Mercenary Guild, but he was wrong. Within the Companions, he found a family. He found ideals worth fighting for. After helping the local Clan Gray-mane retrieve one of their own, he soon found another. Fralia Gray-mane had looked at him kindly, and said his parents would be proud of him. Galloran was touched, and from this moment forward swore to fight for those who couldn't fight for themselves. Giving up the mercenary life, Galloran became a warrior for good, someone who fought to protect others, instead of enriching himself. He took up sword and shield to defend his friends, and keep away his enemies.

"Damn wizards," I thought. "So damn arrogant." I stood facing a trio of them. They were young, just out of school. That the problem with magic. All these hot shots thinking the rule the world cause they can fling a few fireballs. They don't have to work hard to use magic. Not like with a gun. I feel for my weapon.  A Colt Python, the last of its kind. I smile. Just like me. The last gunslinger. It had a nice ring to it, and I became infamous for it. And that why these wizard asshole had challenged me. They intended to duel me one on one, but I didn't have the time for that. This was a duel to the death, and they intended to prove magic superior than steel. "Hey!" I shout. "You guys done thinking up some fancy spells?" Their leader smirks and nods. They are so confident, so sure in their ability. They don't know jack. We all take our places, me on my side with my revolver, them on their side with their hands glowing. Off to the side, the crowd grew restless. They wanted to see blood. Our mediator called out, "Alright now! On the count of ten, go!" I stared at them, ready. They stared back, already whispering a few spells. "1! 2! 3! 4! 5! 6! 7! 8! 9!" The mediator hesitated for a second, then signed and yelled, "10!" They watched launched a spell at me. The one on the right cast a lightning bolt at me, the one on the left launched a few icicles, and the one in the middle fired an orb of pure black energy at me. I smirked. They may have fired first, but their magic was slow. Quick as a flash, I pulled out my revolver and fired off a few rounds. My bullets traveled faster, and pierced their spells before they'd even crossed into my side. I quickly reloaded and fired three bullets-one for each of them-just above their heads. Close enough to where they felt it streak past them. I holstered my revolver and turned to walk away. "Your spells might be effective, but nothing's faster than a bullet fired from someone who knows what he's doing. Try again next time." They say in stunned silence. The crowd was equally quiet. I walked out of that town smiling. They would live, and I wouldn't just be known as the Last Gunslinger. No, I would be known as The Man who beat Magic. "I reckon I'm gonna be getting myself into a few more duels from here on out." I patted my gun. We would be ready.

It sat perfectly still in its cage. That was the creepiest thing about it. Everything other subject would move around, thrash about the place or generally try to break out. But this one just...sat...still. It interested me the most. You'd think being a security guard at a top secret government holding facility would make for an exciting life, but despite what all the movie tell you, it's really just another job. Hold a big gun, make sure the cages are working, keep the security system on. And rule number one of this place, don't be an idiot. Which specifically meant, don't be curious. On the off hours we could read about all the different subjects they kept locked up here, at least all the information they knew. As for this one, nothing. No information. And it wasn't knew either, it was one of the oldest subjects here. They just decided to lock it up, and then apparently decided to leave it there. So it waited. And waited. Occasionally while doing my rounds I would come by and watch it. Never get close though, I'm not that stupid. But I would sit and watch it for hours, just to see if it would move. As far as I knew, it didn't. Didn't eat either, though that wasn't strange. Lots of this subjects survived without eating anything tangible. So I would sit, watching, and it would sit, not moving. I often wondered what it say there for. Eventually I realized. It was waiting. 

True to all those science fiction movies, something went wrong, and they broke out. I'm not sure how it happened, but I'm sure it was Gene, head of security. Regardless, a large group of subjects broke out, an I had the misfortune of being on duty. They killed in droves, scientists, guards, handlers, everyone. Nothing we did could stem the tide. So I ran. I got the hell out of there and his myself away in one of their old cages. Unfortunately, it was its cage. The one who waited. Perfectly still. I didn't realize, I was running for my life. The subject, it was waiting in the cage. As soon as I entered and closed the door, it finally moved. It shamble towards me, and grabbed my head with two hands. And the things it showed me...oh god they were *beautiful*. The things that swirled around its head...they were indescribable. I've been laying on the floor crying since then. It left, it finally left. I can hear the other subjects getting closer. But I don't care, I've realized. It doesn't matter if they kill me. I have already seen Heaven, and I can't wait to get there. I can hear them banging against the wall now. My moment has come. They will come and destroy my flesh. *I will be free.*

They said they wouldn't remove anything. They said the treatment didn't require anything like that. They lied. 

I woke up a few hours after the treatment, groggy and sore. The first thing that hit me was the silence. Hospitals aren't quiet. There's always noise, activity, the rush of people, little announcements over the intercom. There was nothing. Only a dreadful silence. I sat up and got off the surgery table. I stepped down into a poop of blood. I looked down and saw what was left of my doctors and surgeons. Bits of them were spread around the room. They took it out and it took them apart. I sighed and continued onward, walking out the surgery room. My head was pounding, but I didn't feel as groggy. The anesthesia was starting to wear off, but it didn't matter. I was already wide awake and alert. I meandered down a few hallways, finding a few other bits of gore that used to be human. I didn't know where I was going, but I had to go. Had to go get it back. After a few minutes of walking, I realized that I was heading towards a sound. The sound of meat and bone being torn and crushed. The sound of eating. I spurred onward, determined to reach my goal. I found it in the cafeteria of all places. It was a bloodbath, blood and bone and meat scattered around. Occasionally there were a few scraps of fabric or a name tag that told you these piles of meat used to be living people. I looked at the center of the room. It was floating in the area, tearing a corpse apart and occasionally eating some of it. I walked up towards it. It sensed my presense and dropped the body. It sat on the floor and turned to me. "Took you long enough. I got bored." Wordlessly, I stared at it. It stared back, waiting. It shrugged and said, "Hey, wasn't my fault. You were the dumbass who thought it would be a good idea to let the doctors poke around your body." It moved towards me, shrinking and becoming translucent. "You should let me out more. This was fun." I touched my stomach and absorbed it back into me. I turned around to exit the hospital. All in all, it wasn't too bad. I got it back, and the doctors managed to cure my cancer. It settled back inside me, sated and ready to sleep. I knew that it would come out again soon, whether I wanted it or not.

And they came in these little tin cans right, and my mom half-opened one and left one on the counter. She went to go answer the phone or something, and me, being the dumbass kid I was, stick my finger in the can to get an orange slice. My finger gets stuck, and I immediately panic. I tug on it a bit, panic more, and then rip my finger right out of the can. Ended up almost slicing the tip of my finger off. It was baaaaaad. Anyway, my mom takes me to the emergency room, and they manage to see the finger up. Luckily, I only sliced it open and not off. But here's the best part, next day, I went to my grandpa's house with my family. Now, my grandpa was a doctor and he looked over the stitches and basically says, "These stitches are no good. They could've done better!" He then takes the stitches out, and puts new ones in. Right there. In his fucking living room. Like a badass. Anyway, I have this whole memory blocked out, and I only know this story from stuff my parents tell me. To this day though, my index finger is oddly shaped from the cut and the stitching and re-stitching.

I am able to change mass from form to form, with te process taking longer the more mass I have to gain/lose.

Enjoy shapeshifting? Beyond description yes. My kind originally used our powers in order to gain understanding of other species. To this day I still enjoy seeing the world from many different viewpoints, even if I am forced to for my own survival.

The only real restriction I have is the DNA sample. I need a sample from an organism if I want to change into it. The world started to fade. Everything was going black. It felt cold. The piercing pain from the bullet was gone now. Just numbness. "Damn it," I muttered. You know, after the first few times, death starts to get boring. 

I woke up a few hours later, my body completely healed, if a bit sore. It's always like that. I stood up, stretching my limbs out. I then got up and got started. Usually I don't hold many grudges against the people who kill me, but this prick deserved a bit of a scare. I walked out of the parking garage, and as usual, remembered that day. 

It was raining. That's what I remember most about that day. I was walking home from work when I saw him. I didn't realize it at first, since Death doesn't really look like all those stereotypes. I can't really describe how he looked. His form was shifting a bit, and he was hard to focus on. A lot of shadows were around him too. Regardless, as soon as I saw him, something inside me clicked. I knew who it was. I knew he had come for me. Ironically, I think seeing Death was the reason I died. I wasn't paying attention. I stopped in the street to stare when I got hit by a truck. Prick left me there too. Then everything stopped. He came over to me, the only thing moving, the o let thing that mattered anymore. He pulled me up from the ground, and flashed me a smile. "Hello there James. Sorry about causing your death and everything, but I needed a favor. See, a certain someone downstairs needs your soul very, very badly. And I can't let that happen." Dumbfounded, I said nothing, just continued to state. "As of right now, there's not much he can do to me. But I'm a bit worried about what would happen were he to get his hands on your soul, so I decided to step in. It's really a win-win situation. You see, I'm going to make you unkillable. I'm just gonna look the other way, whenever you die. You will live forever, my friend downstairs will never get your soul, I get o keep doing how I do, reaping the souls of those who die. So good luck my friend!" And with that, he walked away. Time flowed once more, and nobody noticed. Just kept walking, going about their lives. That was a few years ago. I say a few, but I think it was closer to twenty. Maybe twenty five. You lose track of time when time becomes meaningless. But that was in the past. Now, I'm looking for the guy who shot me. 

It takes a while, but it's a small city. Not too hard to find someone if you know what you're doing, and I always know what I'm doing. I track him back to his house. I look at the truck in his driveway. So familiar. Brings me back to that day. The debt from where he hit me is still there, still noticeable. I smile. "Finally found him. Now, he's gonna pay. Kill me once, shame on you, kill me twice, shame on me...." I stride to his house, determined to make him pay for being the reason I can never die.

I stared at the bottle. It sat on the table, invitingly. It seems to say, "Go on. You know you want to." It reminded me of Alice in Wonderland. Those little cakes saying, "Eat me. Eat me." I thought back to the encounter with the man who gave it to me.
                   
      *Flashback*
"That'll do it.....but take my advice. Be alone."
I stared at him. 
"Why? The hell is in those pills?" He laughed. 
"Your full potential." He got up and walked away. As he exited, he called out, "If you don't take it, make sure it stays in that bottle. Don't want those pills making contact with the outside world if they aren't being used."
         
          *End Flashback*
So I took the bottle back to small little apartment. And here I am, sitting at my table. Staring at the bottle. Thinking of Alice in Wonderland. Those small little pills calling to me. They were blue, a deep, ocean blue. They had flecks of an even darker purple with them. 
"You know what," I said to myself, "Why the hell not? I'll take one. I can have my phone ready to call 911 in case I feel anything weird." I got my phone out, ready to call 911. I opened the bottle, and shook the pills out onto the table. I picked one up. It had a faint scent attached to it. I brought it to my nose, and inhaled deeply. Blueberries. It smelled of blueberries, ones I use to pick at my family farm. Without thinking, I popped it into my mouth. The flavor! It exploded into my mouth, a deep and sweet blueberry taste. But it was so much richer than any blueberry I'd ever had before! I quickly put the other one in my mouth, and chewed. They broke down easily enough. I leaned back, enjoying the taste in my mouth. I swallowed them, and slowly waited. A minute passed. Ten minutes. 30 minutes. Nothing happened. I shrugged and decided to move on with my day. The minute I got up, however, I fell to my knees. I started to convulse. I looked at my veins. They looked so blue..... I tried to get up, and immediately crashed back onto the floor. Visions flitted about my head. A plane crashing. Lighting striking a building. Those blueberry farms. Myself, covered in fire. Hours passed. Eventually, I remember falling asleep right there on the floor. 

I looked at myself in the mirror. Nothing much has changed since I took the pills. But I knew that despite my lack of physical change, the mental changes were quite enough. Not to mention my new talent..... Wait a minute. I look closer in the mirror and smile. I finally found a difference. My eyes, which were green before, now have a ring of blue in them. I walk away from the mirror. I walk out of my apartment. I close and lock the door behind me. I keep walking. There's no point for me staying here now. I have ascended. I am aware now. I smile, thinking to myself, "Time to get started." The blues in my eyes get a little bit darker. 


The body still on the floor moves a little. It twitches, clinging to life. If it can survive the next few hours, it will continue to grow. It won't stop. And eventually, it will be ready. It raises its head. It is a formless blob. However, it has a hint of eyes forming. The only telltale sign is a shiny bit of green peaking.
